title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 5 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Corinthians chapter 5 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 5 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Corinthians Chapter 5.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 5, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: We know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved
For in this we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed
Now he that hath wrought us for the selfsame thing is God
For we walk by faith, not by sight
questions.correctAnswer: We know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved
questions.explanation: This statement is found in 2 Corinthians 5:1, which is the first verse of the chapter.

questions.question: What do we have if our earthly house is dissolved?
questions.correctAnswer: A building of God
questions.explanation: This is stated in 2 Corinthians 5:1, which mentions that we have a building of God if our earthly house is dissolved.

questions.question: What do we earnestly desire to be clothed with?
options: Our house which is from heaven
questions.correctAnswer: Our house which is from heaven
questions.explanation: According to 2 Corinthians 5:2, we earnestly desire to be clothed with our house which is from heaven.

questions.question: What condition is mentioned for being found not naked?
questions.correctAnswer: Being clothed
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:3 states that if we are to be found not naked, we must be clothed.

questions.question: What do we groan for while in this tabernacle?
questions.correctAnswer: To be clothed upon
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:4 indicates that we groan, not to be unclothed, but to be clothed upon.

questions.question: Who has wrought us for the selfsame thing?
questions.correctAnswer: God
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:5 clearly states that it is God who has wrought us for the selfsame thing.

questions.question: What have we received from God?
questions.correctAnswer: The earnest of the Spirit
questions.explanation: According to 2 Corinthians 5:5, God has given us the earnest of the Spirit.

questions.question: What are we confident about while at home in the body?
options: We are absent from the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: We are absent from the Lord
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:6 states that while we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord.

questions.question: By what do we walk, according to 2 Corinthians 5?
questions.correctAnswer: By faith
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:7 tells us that we walk by faith, not by sight.

questions.question: Are we to be unclothed or clothed according to our desires?
questions.correctAnswer: Clothed
questions.explanation: The desire expressed in 2 Corinthians 5:4 is to be clothed upon, not to be unclothed.

questions.question: Is it stated that we have a temporary building of God?
questions.correctAnswer: No
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:1 states that we have a building of God that is eternal in the heavens, not temporary.

questions.question: True or False: We groan for our house which is from heaven.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This is affirmed in 2 Corinthians 5:2 where it states we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house which is from heaven.

questions.question: True or False: God has given us the spirit of fear.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This is not stated in the text; rather, 2 Corinthians 5:5 mentions God has given us the earnest of the Spirit, not a spirit of fear.

questions.question: True or False: We walk by sight.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:7 explicitly states that we walk by faith, not by sight.

questions.question: True or False: We are at home with the Lord while in the body.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: According to 2 Corinthians 5:6, while we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord.

medium.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 5 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Corinthians Chapter 5 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 5:8, what are believers confident and willing to do?
options: To be absent from the body and present with the Lord
To remain in the body forever
questions.correctAnswer: To be absent from the body and present with the Lord
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:8 states believers are confident and willing to be absent from the body and present with the Lord.

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 5:9 promise will happen if someone labors as instructed in 2 Corinthians 5:8?
options: They may be accepted of Him
They will be free from judgment
questions.correctAnswer: They may be accepted of Him
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:9 explains that whether present or absent, labor is done so that one may be accepted of Him, connecting to the willingness in 5:8.

questions.question: What must all appear before according to 2 Corinthians 5:10?
questions.correctAnswer: The judgment seat of Christ
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:10 clearly states that all must appear before the judgment seat of Christ.

questions.question: How does knowing the terror of the Lord, as mentioned in 2 Corinthians 5:11, affect Paul's approach to persuading men?
options: It compels him to persuade men
It causes him to avoid confrontation
It leads him to only teach privately
questions.correctAnswer: It compels him to persuade men
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:11 shows Paul knows the terror of the Lord and therefore is motivated to persuade men.

questions.question: Why does Paul say in 2 Corinthians 5:12 that he does not commend himself again to the Corinthians?
options: To give them occasion to glory on his behalf
Because he no longer cares for them
Because he wants to remain humble
questions.correctAnswer: To give them occasion to glory on his behalf
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:12 states Paul does not commend himself again but wants them to have something to answer those who glory in appearance, not heart.

questions.question: What does Paul mean in 2 Corinthians 5:13 when he says, 'whether we be beside ourselves, it is to God'?
options: His actions, even if extreme, are directed toward God
He is ashamed of his behavior
questions.correctAnswer: His actions, even if extreme, are directed toward God
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:13 clarifies that whether Paul acts unusually or soberly, it is ultimately to God’s purpose and for their cause.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 5:14, what constrains Paul and his companions?
questions.correctAnswer: The love of Christ
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:14 explicitly states that the love of Christ is what constrains Paul and his companions.

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 5:1 describe as a building of God?
options: A house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens
questions.correctAnswer: A house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:1 contrasts our earthly house with a building of God not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 5:5 say God has given as a guarantee for what He has wrought us for?
questions.correctAnswer: The earnest of the Spirit
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:5 states God has given us the earnest of the Spirit as a guarantee for the purpose He has wrought us for.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 5:6 describe the believer’s confidence while at home in the body?
options: Confident, knowing we are absent from the Lord
Confident, knowing we are present with the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: Confident, knowing we are absent from the Lord
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:6 explains that while at home in the body, believers are confident, knowing they are absent from the Lord.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 5:7, how do believers walk?
questions.correctAnswer: By faith, not by sight
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:7 states believers walk by faith and not by sight.

questions.question: What is the reason for groaning in 2 Corinthians 5:4?
options: Being burdened, desiring mortality to be swallowed up of life
questions.correctAnswer: Being burdened, desiring mortality to be swallowed up of life
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:4 explains groaning is due to being burdened, not wanting to be unclothed but clothed so mortality is swallowed up of life.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Corinthians 5:14 teaches that Christ’s love motivates believers because He died for all, making all alive in Him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:14 says the love of Christ constrains believers, judging that since one died for all, all were dead, implying new life in Him.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Corinthians 5:10, only believers will appear before the judgment seat of Christ to receive rewards.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:10 states 'we must all appear' before the judgment seat of Christ, indicating everyone, not only believers, will appear.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Corinthians 5:9 encourages believers to labor so that they may be accepted by men.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:9 says believers labor to be accepted of Him (God), not men.

hard.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 5 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Corinthians Chapter 5.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 5:15, why did Christ die for all?
options: So that those who live should live unto him who died for them and rose again
To establish a new covenant with Israel
To demonstrate the power of the Spirit
To fulfill the law of Moses
questions.correctAnswer: So that those who live should live unto him who died for them and rose again
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:15 states that Christ died for all so that those who live should not live unto themselves but unto him who died for them and rose again.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 5:16, Paul says 'henceforth know we no man after the flesh.' What does this signify?
options: That believers now perceive others spiritually rather than by outward appearance
That Paul rejects all physical relationships
That knowledge of Christ is limited to His human nature
That fleshly desires must be suppressed
questions.correctAnswer: That believers now perceive others spiritually rather than by outward appearance
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:16 explains that knowing no man after the flesh means that believers now see others spiritually, no longer judging based on external or fleshly appearances.

questions.question: What transformation happens to anyone 'in Christ' according to 2 Corinthians 5:17?
options: They become a new creature; old things pass away and all things become new
They gain wealth and power in this world
questions.correctAnswer: They become a new creature; old things pass away and all things become new
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:17 clearly states that if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creature, with old things passed away and all things become new.

questions.question: What ministry has God given us, as per 2 Corinthians 5:18?
questions.correctAnswer: The ministry of reconciliation
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:18 states that God hath reconciled us to Himself by Jesus Christ and hath given us the ministry of reconciliation.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 5:19, what is God’s attitude towards the trespasses of the world?
options: Not imputing their trespasses unto them
questions.correctAnswer: Not imputing their trespasses unto them
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:19 states that God was in Christ reconciling the world unto Himself, not imputing their trespasses unto them.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 5:20, believers are called ambassadors for Christ. What is the role of an ambassador in this context?
options: To beseech others to be reconciled to God
To lead armies in spiritual warfare
questions.correctAnswer: To beseech others to be reconciled to God
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:20 describes believers as ambassadors for Christ, beseeching others to be reconciled to God, representing God’s appeal.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'katallassō' in 2 Corinthians 5:18 mean?
options: To reconcile or restore to favor
questions.correctAnswer: To reconcile or restore to favor
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'katallassō' in 2 Corinthians 5:18 means 'to reconcile' or 'to restore to favor,' referring to God’s act of reconciling believers to Himself.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in 2 Corinthians 5:21 where Christ is made 'to be sin for us'?
questions.correctAnswer: Typology
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:21 uses typology, portraying Christ as a sin-bearer foreshadowed by Old Testament sacrificial systems where an innocent substitute bore the sins of others.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is closely connected to Paul's teaching in 2 Corinthians 5:21 about Christ bearing sin?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah 53:6
questions.explanation: Isaiah 53:6 describes the suffering servant bearing the iniquities of many, which is echoed in 2 Corinthians 5:21 where Christ is made sin for us.

questions.question: Which New Testament verse echoes the theme of reconciliation found in 2 Corinthians 5:19?
questions.correctAnswer: Colossians 1:20
questions.explanation: Colossians 1:20 speaks of God reconciling all things to Himself through Christ, echoing the reconciliation theme in 2 Corinthians 5:19.

questions.question: What verse immediately precedes 2 Corinthians 5:15?
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Corinthians 5:14
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:14 directly precedes verse 15 and introduces the love of Christ as the constraining force leading to the conclusions in verse 15.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'old things are passed away' in 2 Corinthians 5:17 in the context of Pauline theology?
options: It signifies the believer’s death to the old self and the resurrection to new life in Christ
It implies that the Mosaic law is still in effect
It means that all worldly possessions are lost
It refers to the destruction of the temple
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies the believer’s death to the old self and the resurrection to new life in Christ
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:17 uses this phrase to denote the transformation of believers, reflecting Pauline themes of dying with Christ to old sin and rising to new spiritual life.

questions.question: How does Paul describe the change in perception of knowing others 'after the flesh' in 2 Corinthians 5:16, and what might this imply about Christian identity?
options: Knowing others spiritually rather than by external traits, implying a new identity in Christ
Rejecting all former relationships, implying isolation
Judging others by their social status, implying exclusivity
Focusing on physical lineage, implying ethnic priority
questions.correctAnswer: Knowing others spiritually rather than by external traits, implying a new identity in Christ
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:16 indicates that after coming to Christ, believers perceive others through a spiritual lens, which aligns with the new identity in Christ transcending fleshly distinctions.

questions.question: What theological theme is illustrated by the phrase 'that mortality might be swallowed up of life' in 2 Corinthians 5:4?
options: Victory over death and the promise of resurrection life
questions.correctAnswer: Victory over death and the promise of resurrection life
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:4 contains the phrase indicating that mortality (death) will be overcome by life, reflecting the Christian hope of resurrection and eternal life.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Corinthians 5:21, Jesus was made sin for us despite having known sin.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:21 states that Jesus 'knew no sin,' meaning He was sinless though made sin for us.

theological.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 5 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Corinthians Chapter 5 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 5:17 teach about salvation?
options: Regeneration resulting in a new creation
questions.correctAnswer: Regeneration resulting in a new creation
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:17 states that if any man is in Christ, he is a new creature, indicating the doctrine of regeneration and newness of life in salvation.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 5:21 teach about the nature of Christ's atonement?
options: Christ was punished for sins He did not commit
Christ's death was an example of moral teaching
Christ's righteousness is imputed to believers
Christ was only a moral exemplar
questions.correctAnswer: Christ's righteousness is imputed to believers
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:21 explains that Christ was made sin for us so that we might be made the righteousness of God in Him, teaching the imputation of Christ's righteousness.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 5:18 teach about the ministry of believers?
options: Believers are called to the ministry of reconciliation
Believers should focus solely on worship
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are called to the ministry of reconciliation
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:18 teaches that God has given believers the ministry of reconciliation, highlighting their role in God's redemptive plan.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Corinthians 5:5 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Providence
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:5 shows God's providence in working and preparing believers for eternal life and giving the Spirit as a guarantee.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Corinthians 5:19 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:19 reveals God's mercy in reconciling the world to Himself, not imputing their trespasses to them.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 5:1 connect to the broader biblical theme of resurrection and eternal life?
options: It denies the resurrection of the body
It affirms a heavenly, eternal dwelling beyond earthly life
It limits eternal life to earthly existence
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms a heavenly, eternal dwelling beyond earthly life
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:1 describes an eternal house not made with hands in heaven, connecting to the biblical hope of resurrection and eternal life beyond the earthly body.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 5:20 relate to the redemptive-historical role of believers?
options: Believers serve as ambassadors calling others to reconciliation with God
Believers are only to focus on personal piety
Believers must establish a new covenant
questions.correctAnswer: Believers serve as ambassadors calling others to reconciliation with God
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:20 presents believers as Christ's ambassadors, entrusted with beseeching others to be reconciled to God, reflecting their active role in redemptive history.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Corinthians 5:14 and 2 Corinthians 5:15 teach about the motivation for Christian living?
options: The love of Christ compels believers to live for Him who died and rose again
Legalistic adherence to the law is necessary
Believers should live independently of Christ's death
questions.correctAnswer: The love of Christ compels believers to live for Him who died and rose again
questions.explanation: Verses 14 and 15 teach that Christ’s love constrains believers to no longer live for themselves but for Him who died and rose again, emphasizing Christ-centered sanctification.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Corinthians 5:10 and 2 Corinthians 5:11 teach about judgment and evangelism?
options: Judgment motivates believers to persuade others with fear and reverence
Evangelism is a work of human wisdom alone
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment motivates believers to persuade others with fear and reverence
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:10-11 link the reality of appearing before Christ’s judgment seat with the motivation to persuade others, emphasizing reverence and responsibility in evangelism.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Corinthians 5:6 and 2 Corinthians 5:8 teach about the believer's present and future state?
options: Believers are absent from God while in the body
Believers are always present with the Lord even in the body
While living, believers are away from the Lord but desire to be present with Him after death
Believers do not have assurance of presence with the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: While living, believers are away from the Lord but desire to be present with Him after death
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 8 explain that while believers are at home in the body, they are absent from the Lord, but they are confident and willing to be absent from the body to be present with the Lord.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that 2 Corinthians 5:7 teaches Christians to rely on blind faith without any evidence. What does 2 Corinthians 5:7 actually teach?
options: Christians walk by faith, which is trust in God's revealed truth rather than sight
Christians should reject all reasoning and evidence
Faith is irrational and opposed to knowledge
Faith is only emotional and subjective
questions.correctAnswer: Christians walk by faith, which is trust in God's revealed truth rather than sight
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:7 states 'For we walk by faith, not by sight,' meaning believers trust in God's revealed truth beyond immediate sensory evidence, not blind faith.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 5:16 teach about the believer's knowledge of Christ?
options: Believers continue to know Christ only in His human nature
Believers know Christ no longer after conversion
Believers know Christ now spiritually rather than after the flesh
Believers reject any knowledge of Christ
questions.correctAnswer: Believers know Christ now spiritually rather than after the flesh
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:16 indicates that though believers once knew Christ after the flesh, they now know Him no more in that way, reflecting a spiritual knowledge of Christ after conversion.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Corinthians 5:21 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:21 demonstrates God's justice by showing that Christ, who knew no sin, was made sin for us, satisfying the righteous requirements of the law.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Corinthians 5:2 and 2 Corinthians 5:4 teach about the Christian's present sufferings and future hope?
options: Believers groan for heavenly transformation that will swallow up mortality with life
There is no hope beyond this life
Suffering is a sign of God's rejection
questions.correctAnswer: Believers groan for heavenly transformation that will swallow up mortality with life
questions.explanation: Verses 2 and 4 describe believers groaning and desiring to be clothed with the heavenly dwelling so that mortality is swallowed up by life, teaching the hope beyond present suffering.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 5:9 connect to the theme of sanctification in Scripture?
options: Believers do not need to live holy lives
Believers labor to be accepted by God whether present or absent
God accepts believers regardless of their works
questions.correctAnswer: Believers labor to be accepted by God whether present or absent
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:9 teaches that believers labor to be accepted by God, reflecting the biblical theme of sanctification as ongoing effort to live pleasing to God.
